Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:21: Proof that the soul comprises two hundred and forty-eight limbs is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, portion of Terumah 150a) and in several places, that the ruach takes shape in the lower Garden of Eden clothed in the garment of the practical commandments, taking on a form like what it had in this world; and he says (Zohar, Bereishit 7a) that in the lower Garden of Eden the righteous recognize one another, and this is [the meaning of] (Psalms 31:20) "how great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You, wrought for those who trust in You, before the sons of men" - he says that the lower Garden of Eden is "before the sons of men," in that there they recognize one another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:22: Further, they said in Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas 222b) - their words: "what is the reward for the soul in the World to Come? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, clothes it first in clouds of glory; first it enters into a 'vision' [mareh] that is in the likeness of the body, comprised of two hundred and forty-eight limbs, so too it enters into a 'vision' [mareh] comprised of two hundred and forty-eight commandments and of two hundred and forty-eight lights that separate out from that vision" - so far. And it is explained afterward that six hundred and thirteen angels raise up the soul, corresponding to the two hundred and forty-eight positive and three hundred and sixty-five negative commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:23: Since we know that the portion of ruach comprises a complete stature of two hundred and forty-eight limbs, so too the portion of nefesh, which is in the courtyard of death, and the portion of neshamah that ascends to the supernal Garden of Eden - each of them is comprised of two hundred and forty-eight spiritual limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:24: With this introduction we understand the matter of sin, which is fittingly called a "corpse" [chalal] in the soul: just as an enemy who strikes the body of a person with a sword makes it a corpse, so too the sword of Samael, entering the two hundred and forty-eight limbs of the soul, makes it a corpse and defiles it. The reason is that just as the impurity of a corpse comes because the light of the holy soul has departed and the spirit of Samael's impurity rests there, defiling it with a severe impurity, the father of the fathers of impurity, which is the corpse - so too the sinner removes from himself the holy soul and Samael rests in its place, and therefore it defiles like a corpse; for this reason the wicked, even in their lifetimes, are called "dead" (Bereishit Rabbah 39:7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:25: To understand why it is called "a corpse" and not "death" in the soul: the matter is that a living person who is killed is called a "corpse" [chalal] because the life of the blood has been removed from him, for the blood is the nefesh, and the body remains a corpse without life. The term "chalal" is used as in (Exodus 31:14) "those who profane [mechaleleha] it shall surely be put to death," as is explained in the portion of Bereishit (6a) regarding one who blemishes an inner point, so that that place remains a "corpse"; and likewise the matter of sin blemishing the essence of the soul, which is in the heart - there it makes it a corpse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:26: The rule is that from the physical we understand the spiritual: any wound by which a person is struck such that he dies from that wound makes him a "corpse"; so too, sin, according to its magnitude, in the limb it has blemished in his soul, is called a "corpse" in the soul. It is called a corpse because the soul is holy and sin is the darkening of the spirit of impurity from Samael, and according to the entry of the spirit of impurity into the soul, its spirituality departs, and that place remains a corpse, without spirituality.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:27: This is the matter of the blemish, for the word "pegam" [blemish] means a deficiency - that the light is diminished in that place, and darkness rules there from Samael. Therefore, one who blemishes his eyes darkens the eyes of his soul, and if, because of the magnitude of the blemish, he must come back in reincarnation, he must be blind, and darkness and the clouds of Samael must rule over his eyes, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Tikkunim (50a) - his words: "Samael - darkness, serpent, gloom - of him it is said (Isaiah 50:3) 'I clothe the heavens with blackness' - his female counterpart - 'and I make sackcloth their covering.' Woe to the soul when it is clothed in their gloom, of which it is said (Genesis 27:1) 'and his eyes grew dim from seeing' - these are the darknesses that cover the eyes, that have no permission to gaze upon the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah; of the light and lamp that shine within them it is said (Ecclesiastes 12:3) 'and those who look through the windows grow dark,' as Ecclesiastes says (12:2) 'before the sun and the light... grow dark'; and of light and lamp it is said (Proverbs 6:23) 'for the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light.' And why do they grow dark within them? Because they did not occupy themselves with Torah and mitzvah in the fear and love which are Yud-Heh [of the Divine Name]; and as soon as they occupy themselves with them in fear and love, an oath is sworn by the Holy One, blessed be He, to remove them [the darknesses] from the world, and the soul, because of the darknesses, separates between Yud-Heh and Vav-Heh; and at the time when the darknesses are removed from the soul, immediately 'let every soul praise Yah.' And who are these darknesses? These are Samael and the serpent. And who causes them to rule? Rather, the secret of the verse teaches (Isaiah 59:2) 'but your iniquities have separated between you and your God'; and David, because of them, said (Psalms 119:18) 'open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of Your Torah' - at that time, whereas the darknesses ruled over the lights of the eyes, the lights are transformed and rule over the darknesses" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:28: Here it is explained in this passage that Samael and the serpent are the darknesses that darken the eyes, and this is on account of sin, as it says, "for your iniquities have separated," etc.; and incidentally it is explained in the passage that the cause of the darkening of the eyes is also because they did not occupy themselves with Torah and mitzvah in fear and love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:29: Let us return to our discourse: every blemish a person causes is a blemish to the soul and darkens its light, and for this reason sin is called "a corpse in the soul" for the reason explained. Now, according to this, we may say that every single sin a person blemishes is called "a corpse" - meaning either a lesser death or a greater death, all of which are called "death," along the lines of "a poor man is considered as dead" and other cases our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Nedarim 64b), where the cause of the withdrawal of one's flow and light is called "death." So too, in the matter of "corpse," any withdrawal of the light of the soul on account of sin, leaving that place a corpse into which Samael may enter, is called "a corpse in the soul."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:30: Now that it has been explained that sin darkens the soul, we understand by this what our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, quoted in the Yalkut (Psalms, chapter 68, remez 795), on the verse (Psalms 68:12) "the Lord gives the word" - it is taught, Rashbi: before Adam sinned, he would hear the Voice and stand on his feet, as it is said (Genesis 3:8) "and they heard the voice of the Lord God"; but once he sinned, he heard and hid, as it is said (ibid.) "and the man hid himself." Before Israel sinned, what is written? (Exodus 24:17) "and the appearance of the glory of the Lord was like a devouring fire" - Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said, seven partitions of fire were sparkling one against another, and Israel would see and not fear and not be afraid; but once they sinned, they could not even look upon the face of the intermediary [Moses], as it is said (Exodus 34:30) "and Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, and behold, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come near him" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:31: The reason for this is that when the soul is pure and bright it can gaze into the light, in the manner of one who stands in the light, whom the sunlight does not harm; but one who stands in darkness and the sunlight strikes his eyes cannot endure it, and recoils and turns back and shuts his eyes. So too Israel, at the giving of the Torah, the filth of their sin ceased and their soul was purified through the counting of the seven weeks for their purification, and three days before receiving the Torah they were warned not to approach a woman, as it is said (Exodus 19:15) "be ready for the third day; do not approach a woman," and they washed their garments through immersion - all these good preparations to purify their soul to receive the Torah; and through this they were able to gaze; but when they sinned, they returned to draw upon themselves the filth and darkness of the serpent and darkened their soul, until they could not gaze even upon the face of the intermediary.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:1: One must fear lest his soul be cast outward when it ascends above upon its departure from this world, as Rashbi explains (Zohar, Pinchas 213b), on the verse (Psalms 86:2) "guard [shomrah] my soul, for I am pious" - his words: "'Guard my soul' - it should have said 'guard' [shemor, in the standard form]; and we have learned that there is not a single letter in the Torah that does not contain supernal and precious secrets. 'Shomrah' [interpreted: 'she guards'] - he says this to the Holy One, blessed be He, referring to that portion [i.e., the Shechinah] with which my soul is united, for when the soul departs from this world, it comes to inherit the world; if it merits, many supernal hosts go out to receive it and to guard it and to bring it into the abode of its place, and this Heh [the Shechinah] guards it, to unite with it at the New Moons and Sabbaths; but if it does not merit, several guardians of impure spirits are ready to receive it and push it outward. Woe to that soul that is tossed about empty, like a stone in a sling, as it is said (I Samuel 25:29) 'and the souls of your enemies He shall sling out from the hollow of a sling.' And David sought his petition before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said, 'guard my soul,' that it not be pushed outward; and when it comes to receive it, may they open gates for it and receive it before You" - so far. And if David the king, peace be upon him, needed to pray that his soul not be pushed outward, how much more must one full of countless sins fear his sins and hasten to repentance and prayer, before the day comes when regret will no longer avail.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:2: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 3b): Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan: whoever performs one mitzvah in this world, it precedes him and walks before him in the World to Come, as it is said (Isaiah 58:8) "and your righteousness shall walk before you"; and whoever commits one transgression in this world, it wraps itself around him and walks before him to the Day of Judgment, as it is said (Job 6:18) "the paths of their way turn aside; they go up into the waste and are lost." Rabbi Elazar says, it is bound to him like a dog, as it is said (Genesis 39:10) "and he did not listen to her, to lie beside her, to be with her" - "to lie beside her" in this world, "to be with her" in the World to Come - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:3: The matter of "it wraps itself around him and walks before him to the Day of Judgment" is because whoever commits one transgression acquires for himself one accuser, and each and every accuser has the measure of a complete stature - just as with a mitzvah, so with a transgression. Now, the two hundred and forty-eight mitzvot are the measure of the stature of the supernal Adam, two hundred and forty-eight holy limbs, and every mitzvah contains a hint of YHVH, as is explained in the Tikkunim (73a, 131b) and Ra'aya Meheimna (see Pinchas 228b), for a mitzvah [numerically, via a particular method] equals YHVH, and YHVH is the totality of the whole stature - except that within each and every limb is the totality of everything. Therefore, whoever fulfills one mitzvah properly is as though he fulfilled them all, as I explained above in chapter 4 in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and he thereby fashions one complete angel of two hundred and forty-eight limbs, who is his defender.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:4: Of this kind is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 12) concerning Adam, the first man, that he contained all the souls within him - some hanging from the hairs of his head, some from his arm, some from his body, some from his legs, etc. Now, just as every soul is comprised of two hundred and forty-eight limbs and is nonetheless [associated with] a portion of a particular limb, so every accuser, once it is made through the power of this person, in the power of all two hundred and forty-eight limbs, has two hundred and forty-eight limbs and is a portion of a particular limb of the stature of Samael.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:5: This is [the meaning of] "do not say, I will repay evil" (Proverbs 20:22), which is explained in the Zohar, portion of Mikeitz (201a): do not say that you will complete "the evil," which is Samael, through your sins, to give him a complete stature. And it says: he, this repugnant one, is completed only through the sins of human beings; therefore a person must be careful not to let that evil inclination be completed through his sins, and to always guard himself, for the good inclination wishes to complete him in completeness always, and not the evil inclination; therefore, "do not say, I will repay evil; wait for the Lord and He will save you" - so far. We find, then, that the measure of the whole stature [of the evil force] is completed through many evil deeds, but each and every sin, and each portion of a limb from it, is comprised of two hundred and forty-eight, as I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:6: With this introduction we understand "it wraps itself around him and walks before him to the Day of Judgment" - meaning that it wraps around him entirely and becomes a garment for his soul to bring it into Gehinnom, until that ugliness and darkness in the soul is digested. This is the matter of the filthy garments that Rashbi explains (Pinchas 214a) they clothe the soul with to bring it into Gehinnom - his words: "Rabbi Elazar opened and said (Zechariah 3:1) 'and he showed me Joshua the High Priest standing before the angel of the Lord,' etc. Come and see, woe to those people who do not gaze upon the honor of their Master, and every single day a herald calls out over them and they do not heed it. If a person comes to gaze at the commandments of the Torah, how many defenders stand ready to speak well of him! If a person comes and transgresses the commandments of the Torah, they become accusers against him, speaking ill of him before the Holy One, blessed be He. Joshua was the High Priest, as we have established; what is written of him? 'And Satan stood at his right hand to accuse him.' And if this is so for him, how much more so for the rest of the world's inhabitants, who do not gaze upon their Master.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:7: See what is written of him: 'and Joshua was clothed in filthy garments,' as we have established - but the filthy garments are certainly the garments in which the spirit is clothed in that world; and it has been said that whoever is destined to enter Gehinnom, these are the garments they clothe him in - how so? What is written here? 'And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments and standing before the angel' - which angel is this? The angel appointed over Gehinnom, appointed over whoever is seen in those garments - until he answered and said, 'remove the filthy garments from upon him.' From here we may understand that a person's deeds make for him those filthy garments; and it says to him, 'see, I have removed your iniquity from you, and I will clothe you with fine apparel' - I will clothe him with other, proper garments, in which a person gazes upon the splendor of his Master's glory" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:8: Here it is explained that a person's deeds are what make for him filthy garments - according to the number of his sins, so is the number of the garments, for each and every sin makes for him a garment; this is [the meaning of] "it wraps itself around him" mentioned in the passage. Proof of this: "see, I have removed your iniquity from you," and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (see Targum, Zechariah) that his iniquity was that his sons had married foreign women.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:9: Rabbi Elazar says it is "bound to him like a dog" - meaning that it does not only make a garment for him, but also cleaves to the soul itself, to become attached to it. It is the way of a dog that bites that its teeth retain a portion of the person, and it is the way of one bitten by a dog to imagine dogs before him, even in his urine, as is observed in practice many times. We find, then, that a portion of the transgression is within the soul itself, and this is the matter of the blemish I explained, which is a "corpse" in the soul; and further, a portion of the soul is left within the transgression, which is the power of Lilith - this is the matter of "bound," a doubled bond, this within that and that within this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:10: The portion of the transgression that he acquires in his soul is what walks with him in this world - this is "to lie beside her in this world." And the portion of his soul that remains in it is to be with it in the World to Come, for Lilith takes hold of him because of that portion that remains in her, to bring him down to Gehinnom. We find, then, that this particular blemish - lying with a gentile woman - is in the matter of the verse mentioned in the story of Joseph; the reason being that through his lying with her, a spirit is placed within her, which is a portion of his soul, and therefore he is compelled to be with her in the World to Come - this is "bound like a dog," as will be explained, with the Lord's help, regarding the meaning of "dog."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:11: Nevertheless, we may say that in every single transgression by which a person becomes defiled through that evil desire, he lies with Lilith, for all the desires of the world are from the power of Lilith; since Samael, due to his extreme subtlety, has no connection allowing him to take hold of man, who is physical, he therefore sends his female counterpart, who is more physical, and she is the one who entices. So too, regarding the seven Palaces of Impurity, which correspond to Lilith, it is explained in the Zohar, portion of Pekudei (262b-268a), that from them spread several enticements to human beings and several pleasures in this world, and she shows him several faces to cause him to sin and to draw him to her. We find, then, that when a person is drawn after the affairs of this world, he is drawn after her, and his soul is bound to him like a dog. Adam, the first man, because he was drawn after the enticements of the serpent, which are the powers of Lilith, caused death for himself and for those who came after him, as is explained in the portion of Pekudei, at the beginning of the Palaces of Impurity (262b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:12: It is explained in the portion of Vayetze, in the Tosefta (148a), that Lilith is the enticer, and Samael does not entice because of his subtlety - his words: "the secret of secrets, from within the power of the noontime of Isaac, came forth from within the dregs of wine a single knot, comprising a male and female, red as a rose, dividing into several sides and paths. The male is called Samael, his female always comprised within him; just as it is so on the holy side, so too on the other side, male and female comprised one within the other. Samael's female is called serpent, a woman of harlotry, the end of all flesh, the end of days. Two evil spirits cleave together as one - the male's spirit is subtle, the female's spirit divides into several ways and paths, and it cleaves to that male spirit. She adorns herself with several ornaments like a harlot who lures from afar, standing at the head of the roads and paths to entice people; the fool who draws near to her, she seizes him and kisses him, gives him to drink the wine of the dregs of the venom of vipers. Once he drinks, he strays after her; after she sees him stray after her from the path of truth, she strips herself of all those ornaments with which she had adorned herself for that fool."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:13: Her ornaments, to entice human beings: her hair is arranged, red as a rose, her face white and red; hanging from her ears are six ornaments imported from Egypt; hanging on her neck are all the ornaments of the ancient land; her mouth is arranged with a delicate opening, beautiful in its adornment, her tongue sharp as a sword, her words smooth as oil, her lips beautiful, red as a rose, sweetened with all the sweetness of the world; she is dressed in purple, adorned with thirty-nine ornaments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:14: The fool who strays after her and drinks from her cup of wine, and commits adultery with her and strays after her - what does she do? She leaves him sleeping in the bed and ascends above and slanders him, and takes permission and descends. That fool awakens and thinks to dally with her as before, but she has removed her ornaments from herself and turns into a mighty warrior standing opposite him, clothed in a garment of blazing fire, with mighty fear that makes his body and soul tremble, naked, full of frightening eyes, a smooth sword in her hand, bitter drops hanging from that sword - she kills that fool and casts him into Gehinnom" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:15: All these are parables - just as Solomon the king, peace be upon him, likened the affairs of the world and its pleasures, which stem from the power of Lilith, to a harlot woman, as it is said (Proverbs 7:10) "and behold, a woman came to meet him, dressed as a harlot, wily of heart," etc., as her words and counsels are explained in the portion of Pekudei, in the Palaces of Impurity (267a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:16: It is explained in the passage we cited, "the male's spirit is subtle," etc., "the female's spirit divides into several paths," etc. - we find that the female spreads out, and all this is according to a supernal pattern, for "this too, corresponding to that, God made": just as above, the male does not act at all except through the female, so below, in the impure powers. And just as above she acts only through the power of the male, so below, and this is [the meaning of] "and it cleaves to that male spirit."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:17: It remains for us to explain a point in the passage: why transgression is likened to a dog and not to a serpent or something else. The matter can be understood from what is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas 224b), which says that just as with the sacrifices, if they [Israel] merited, the form of a fiery lion would descend, crouching upon the altar, and if not, a dog - so too at the departure of the soul - his words: "as our Rabbis established: if they merited, a fiery lion would descend to consume the offerings, and if not, a fiery dog would descend there. So too, when a person dies: if he merited, a form like a lion descends to receive his soul, and if not, a form like a dog - of which David said (Psalms 22:21) 'save my soul from the sword, my only one, from the power of the dog'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:18: To know the reason for this - the lion and the dog - know that it is explained in the portion of Bereishit (6b) that the form of the lion that would descend upon the altar was called Uriel, and it is likewise explained in the portion of Tzav (32b); and my teacher explains that the reason it has the form of a lion is because its nourishment comes from the right, as it is said (Ezekiel 1:10) "and the face of a lion was on the right of all four of them," etc. But we still need to know why it was Uriel who would descend, and it appears that the reason is what Rashbi explains in the sixth of the Holy Palaces (254b), concerning Raphael and Uriel - he explains there that Raphael is in Tiferet, from where healing and life flow downward, and Uriel is in Malchut.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:19: Now, in the portion of Bereishit (51a), on the verse (Deuteronomy 4:24) "for the Lord your God is a consuming fire," it explains that the fire of the Shechinah, which is a consuming fire, was what consumed the offerings - his words: "and this is the secret of the sacrifice, that the smoke rising arouses this bluish light to ignite, and once ignited, it joins with the white light, and the lamp burns in a single union; and because the way of this bluish light is to destroy and consume everything it attaches to beneath it, when the [divine] favor is found and the lamp burns in a single union, then it is written 'and fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering,' etc.; and thus it is known that this lamp burns in a single union" - so far, as relevant to us. Here we find that the descent of the fire was from the Shechinah, in the illumination of Tiferet within her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:20: He says afterward, that after the supernal fire finished consuming the offering, what was the supernal fire consuming [next]? And he says that Israel would cleave through the arousal from below - the priests, Levites, and Israelites, these with the joy of song, these with the desire of the heart, and these with prayer - and the lamp burns and the lights cleave together as one. We find, then, that the fire of Uriel that descended upon the altar was necessarily through the clothing of the Shechinah in it, in the illumination of Tiferet within her; and this is the name of the angel Uriel, explained in the portion of Pekudei (254b), that he is in the Shechinah, comprised of all of them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:21: Now, concerning the departure of the soul of the righteous from this world, Rashbi explains (Vayechi 235a), on the verse (Proverbs 5:15) "drink water from your own cistern, and flowing water from your own well," that then the [divine] union takes place, and the soul becomes as "female waters" within it, see there. If so, it is necessarily the angel Uriel, corresponding to her [the Shechinah], who descends to raise up the soul of the righteous, which is from the power of the masculine, so that through his good deeds he is aroused to union in the manner of what happened with the sacrifice.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:22: Concerning the matter of the dog, it explains there in the portion of Bereishit (Zohar 6b): if they did not merit, a dog would descend, and the name of that dog is Bila'dan, meaning it is not included among mankind, but is a dog, with a dog's face.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:23: Know that "this too, corresponding to that, God made": just as Uriel is the counterpart of the Shechinah for the arousal of good, so Bila'dan, a dog's face, is for the arousal of evil deeds. And without doubt, the offering would not be given over to the dog except when it had a disqualifying blemish, and therefore "you shall cast it to the dogs," as is explained in the Tikkunim (33b, 62b) concerning a disqualified prayer that is given over to the dog. This dog corresponds to Lilith, and therefore his name is Bila'dan, meaning that he denies the providence of the Shechinah, who is called Adonai, and he is "Bila'dan" - "without a master [ein lo adon]." So too the Geonim explained that the names of the ten kelipot mostly indicate a denial of the Godhead, as my teacher, peace be upon him, quoted their words in Sefer HaPardes, in the Gate of Transformations, and this is the insolence of the dogs, who are called "brazen of soul" (Isaiah 56:11). And with this we may offer another explanation of "Uriel": meaning one who acknowledges the providence of God above him - this is Uriel, "the light [or] I have is from God [E-l]," the secret of "and God is angry" (Psalms 7:12), as is explained in the portion of Bemidbar (30b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:24: There is further proof in Ra'aya Meheimna (portion of Naso 124a) that the dog is from the powers of Lilith - his words: "and the evil inclination from the side of the right is called serpent, and from the side of the left, of Esau, whose rank is Samael, it is called dog, the appointed one of Gehinnom who cries 'Give! Give!' - this is [the meaning of] (Proverbs 30:15) 'the leech has two daughters, Give, Give' - and its desire is to consume the impure soul in its fire, Gehinnom. And a spirit of jealousy passed over him and he was jealous of his wife (Numbers 5:14) truly, and she was defiled; and concerning her it is said (Leviticus 21:9) 'and the daughter of a priestly man' - this is Michael - 'if she begins to profane herself by harlotry, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire' - and there that filth is burned and refined like silver refined in fire, and that lead, the filth, is burned and becomes dust and is crushed" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:25: Here it says that the evil inclination, which is from the power of Lilith - as I explained above, that the enticements of the evil inclination are from the side of Lilith - is called, from the side of the right, "serpent," and from the side of the left, "dog"; and it says that this dog is the appointed one of Gehinnom who cries "Give! Give!" And it is already known that the whole reality of Gehinnom and its seven compartments are from the powers of "the strange, foreign woman," as is explained in the portion of Pekudei.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:26: As for its being called "serpent" from the side of the right: we find that the serpent enticed Adam, the first man, and Eve, and that enticement flowed from its right side, "for God knows that on the day you eat of it... you shall be like gods" (Genesis 3:5), etc.; and similarly with the other enticements of the evil inclination, all of which come from the right side, which draws near, showing peace, tranquility, and security - "eat and drink," and the like goods of this world that flow from the right. Afterward it is called "dog," which cries out against him to cast him into Gehinnom, along the lines explained in the passage from the portion of Vayetze quoted above - this is [the meaning of] "it descends and seduces, ascends and accuses, descends and takes the soul" (see Bava Batra 16a and Ein Yaakov there).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:27: Because this dog corresponds to Lilith, David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 22:21) "save my soul from the sword" - this being the sword of Lilith, as is explained in the passage from the portion of Vayetze (148a) - "from the power of the dog, my only one" - referring to the soul that ascends to union, as is explained in the portion of Vayechi (235a), and therefore it is called "my only one" [yechidati], from the language of "union" [yichud]. "Save" - so that the dog not seize it, which is the one who seizes the soul when there is a disqualifying blemish in it - this is what is explained in the passage from the portion of Vayetze, that Lilith is the one who entices him with the affairs of the world and defiles him, and she kills him and casts him into Gehinnom. And do not be puzzled that "dog" is masculine, for from the side of Samael-Esau it is called dog, from the side of the left, as is explained in the passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:28: Because most sins come from the enticements of Lilith, as I have explained, and she is called "dog" in the manner I explained, our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yoma 86b) that one who sins and repeats [his sin] is like a dog that returns to its vomit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:29: Therefore a person must guard himself from this power of wickedness and its enticements, for its whole intent is to trip a person up and ensnare him in its net and cast him into a pit of roaring waters, into the miry clay, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, elaborated in the Palaces of Impurity (Zohar, portion of Pekudei), see there - for by a person's knowing the punishments for these things, he will guard himself from them, and may God help him.
